Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
items.text: Branch has now been sidelined each of the last four weeks, missing Week 9 and 10 before their Week 11 bye, and did not practice at any point this week. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve” list for players who weren’t close to playing. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
items.text: Olmaide Zachcheaus will be Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver behind Drake London, and after that it turns to Chris Blair and Beaux Collins with Zachariah Branch also hurt. This will likely be a situation that forces the Falcons to condense the target tree and throw at their main three of Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Denzel Boston (quad) is questionable for the Browns’ Week 12 game against the Raiders.
items.text: According to Cabot, Boston was a DNP all week but still managed to draw the questionable tag. Given his week’s worth of DNPs, it’s hard to imagine the rookie suiting up on Sunday night, but it sounds like the Browns will give him some additional time to try and heal up before ruling him out. Fantasy managers planning to hold out until a decision is made would be wise to stash Jerry Jeudy or another player from Sunday or Monday night’s games as a pivot off Boston in the event he is ruled out. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said he “wouldn’t anticipate” Romeo Doubs (shoulder) being ready for action yet.
items.text: Doubs was limited in each of the first two practices this week, and we’re guessing he won’t do better than that today based on this statement. Most players on IR will get a questionable tag on their chances to return regardless of the surrounding data, but we’d be surprised if Doubs didn’t sit this week based on what his coach said. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Parker Washington’s injury is “a big opportunity” for Josh Cameron.
items.text: You may have been thinking that Washington’s injury would create BTJ szn, but Coen singled out Cameron when asked about him, saying he’s “been trending. He’s made a lot of plays for this offense and for this team ... Trevor trusts him.” Cameron suddenly surfaces on the FLEX line as an expected Jaguars No. 2 target behind Jakobi Meyers against the Titans on Sunday. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he had no update on Jeremiyah Love (ankle/IR) and would know more on Wednesday.
items.text: Love is eligible to come off injured reserve after this Sunday, but the fact that LaFleur won’t have a real update until Wednesday is probably foreshadowing that it will be at least another week. Love picked up a high-ankle sprain against the Cowboys in Week 8. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Carson Beck (back) will not play in Week 12 against the Commanders.
items.text: Beck will miss a second straight game with his back injury after missing all of practice this week. The rookie QB has dealt with back issues for the majority of the year, but will now set his sights on returning in Week 13 against the Eagles. That said, the Cardinals have a Week 14 bye, which could give them a reason to sideline Beck for at least one more week and let him heal up before returning for the final four games of the regular season. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals in Week 12 against the Commanders.
items.text: Johnson will get the start on Sunday against the Commanders in what will be a “revenge” game for the 40-year-old vet. Although, in fairness to Johnson, a lot of games are revenge games for the well-traveled vet. Things didn’t fare too well for Johnson in his first start of the season against the Chiefs, as he threw for 155 yards and one touchdown on the road, but did a good job of limiting turnovers. He’s nothing more than a QB3/desperation play in 2QB and superflex leagues. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Colston Loveland (knee) is expected to land on injured reserve but “the current belief” is he could return later in the season.
items.text: The Bears are still running Loveland through additional testing and won’t make any final decisions to place him on IR until after those tests are complete, per Schefter. The early news of a sprained knee, however, is mostly good news for the second-year tight end. Loveland will be required to miss a minimum of four games on injured reserve and won’t be eligible to return until Week 18 at the earliest. items.title: Rams TE Tyler Higbee is considered week-to-week with a chest injury he suffered in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
items.text: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the news on Higbee. Higbee will reportedly have “a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs, but as Schefter reported, that decision will be based on “how he heals over the next week.” Where things stand right now, the Rams are currently down three tight ends, with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Davis Allen (ankle) also considered week-to-week after going down in Week 12. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are expected to serve as the top two tight ends in Sean McVay’s 12-heavy personnel, but the team could look to add a free agent
